overview: Resume Bullet Generator is a digital prompt pack that helps students turn vague class, internship, volunteer, or project experience into clear, action-oriented resume bullets. It includes action-verb lists, STAR framing prompts, and questions that help uncover metrics such as hours saved, people reached, or results improved. It is a writing aid, not a guarantee of interviews or job offers.
usecases: A student has only "helped with club events" and needs a bullet showing planning, attendance, and impact.
An internship description is a list of tasks, and the student wants to frame work around a specific problem, action, and result.
A volunteer role has no obvious numbers, so the prompts help estimate scope, frequency, or audience size honestly.
howto: Download the files and open the prompt pack in your preferred notes or writing app.
Paste a vague experience into the STAR prompts and answer the metric-finding questions without exaggerating.
Select an action verb, draft two bullet options, then edit for accuracy and your resume's style.

faq.q: Will this write my resume for me?
faq.a: No; it provides prompts and wording options, but you must choose accurate details and edit the final bullets.

faq.q: Can I use it if I have no metrics?
faq.a: Yes; it includes questions to help estimate honest scope or results, but not every bullet needs a number.
